title: JS API to associate form controls with a form element.

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
### What problem are you trying to solve?

Currently form controls can only be associated with a form element one of two ways.

1. By being nested inside the form element and inside of the same tree scope (aka not nested inside a shadow root).

2. By using the form attribute and an id reference to a form inside the same tree scope[1]

This means that you can never associate a form control with a form element that's in an ancestor tree, and you also sometimes require use of id references.

[1] referencetarget makes this slightly more complicated but it still only allows you to reference in the same tree or to a subtree.

I want to solve this reliance on idrefs / direct nesting in a minimal way that matches similar idref APIs.

### What solutions exist today?

The only real solution that exists today is to just handle behaviours yourself. Take a submit button within a custom element for example. You would just have to intercept the click event on the button and then use JS to submit the form element that you want to be associated with. This this the sort of pattern that Shoelace [follows](https://github.com/shoelace-style/shoelace/blob/25bd8ec776609670a932f21390be59a495df497d/src/components/button/button.component.ts#L180). This prevents usage of selectors such as `:default` on the button though.

Similarly for input elements shoelace has to handle submitting forms on enter key press and go through a whole complicated class to try and replicate the built-in behaviour that an input associated with a form gives you. See [here](https://github.com/shoelace-style/shoelace/blob/25bd8ec776609670a932f21390be59a495df497d/src/components/input/input.component.ts#L296) and [here](https://github.com/shoelace-style/shoelace/blob/next/src/internal/form.ts#L61).

### How would you solve it?

I propose adding a new .formElement property on the various form controls which is an element reflection property (like `.commandForElement`).

```idl
+[CEReactions, Reflect="form"] attribute Element? formElement;
```

I propose making the above IDL change to all the main form control types (HTMLButtonElement, HTMLInputElement, HTMLSelectElement, and HTMLTextAreaElement).
I'm unsure on whether to update HTMLObjectElement, HTMLFieldSetElement and HTMLOutputElement the utility of the form attribute and general association is unclear to me.
I propose *not* making the change to HTMLLabelElement, HTMLOptionElement, HTMLLegendElement as these despite having a .form property do NOT support the form content attribute.

On top of the built-in elements mentioned above a similar change would be made to ElementInternals so that form associated custom elements can be associated with forms programmatically too.

With this new property you can now programmatically associate form controls with an associated form element, even one that's in an ancestor tree.

Below shows a HTML sample that has a form element with a custom element within it. That custom element contains a submit button that's linked via the new setter to the container form.

```html
<form id="form" onsubmit="alert('submitted')">
  <custom-element id="ce">
    <template shadowrootmode=open>
      <style>
        button:default {
            background-color: blue;
            color: contrast-color(blue);
        }
      </style>
      <button id="button">
        Shadow submit button
      </button>
    </template>
  </custom-element>
</form>

<script>
    const button = ce.shadowRoot.querySelector('#button');
    button.formElement = form;
</script>
```

Note it's important that any reflection mechanisms that return elements associated with a form are updated to retarget so as to not leak elements within a shadow root.

One such example is the [form.elements](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/forms.html#dom-form-elements) property.

### Anything else?

I also considered changing the existing `.form` property to include the new behaviour.

Feature detection is possible either way:
`if (Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(HTMLButtonElement.prototype, 'form').set != undefined)` for changing the existing property or  `if ('formElement' in HTMLButtonElement)` for a new property.

The existing .form property returns the form owner which isn't always equivalent to what .formElement would return. If a button is nested in a form with no form attribute, .form == the form element but .formElement is null.

This is part of https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11577 but we wanted to split the different properties out into their own issues to discuss.

Note that while this proposal can be used to solve *some* of the use cases presented in #12150 it is not an alternative to the entire proposal nor is it in conflict with it. Notably even with that proposal it would be still be useful to support setting of a ElementInternals.formElement property.
